knownIssues.title: Tow Mode via Touchscreen Is the Correct Method
knownIssues.detail: Polestar 2 requires Tow Mode to be activated via the center touchscreen (Car Status > Service > Tow Mode) for safe neutral and EPB release. Using the column stalk alone may allow the vehicle to re-engage drive. Always use Tow Mode.

knownIssues.title: FLATBED ONLY — All Variants
knownIssues.detail: All Polestar 2 variants (Standard Range FWD, Long Range Single Motor, Long Range Dual Motor AWD, Performance AWD) are electric drivetrains. Towing with any driven wheels on the ground risks motor damage. Flatbed is the only method.

knownIssues.title: Extremely Rare and High-Value
knownIssues.detail: The Polestar 1 is one of the rarest vehicles you will ever tow — approximately 1,500 were produced total. It has a carbon fiber body. Use a flatbed with padded ramps and soft tie-down straps. Do not use metal chains or hooks against any body surface.

knownIssues.title: Carbon Fiber Body — Metal Equipment Will Cause Damage
knownIssues.detail: Polestar 1 has a carbon fiber reinforced plastic body. Never use metal chains, hooks, or hard straps directly on body panels. Only padded soft ramps and rubber-lined straps. Approximately 1,500 total units were ever built.

knownIssues.title: Carbon Fiber Body — Extreme Value — ~1,500 Units Produced
knownIssues.detail: The Polestar 1 is a limited production PHEV with a carbon fiber body. Approximately 1,500 units were produced worldwide. Never place metal equipment against the body. Use padded flatbed ramps, rubber-lined straps, and treat this as one of the highest-value vehicles you will encounter.
